description: THE SAME DECLINE, SPELLED IN LOWER CASE - WHEN 'n' at app/cbl/COBIL00C.cbl:179 of the ordered EVALUATE CONFIRMI at :173-191, the lower-case half of the WHEN pair whose body is :180-181. SERVICE. It is the paired counterpart of case13 and differs from it in EXACTLY ONE INBOUND CHARACTER: the confirmation arrives as 'n' rather than 'N'. Every other member is carried over from case13 byte for byte, deliberately, because that is what makes the pair an isolation of the two stacked clauses rather than two loosely similar cases - if anything else moved, a failure here would no longer tell you which clause was at fault. WHY A LOWER-CASE CASE EXISTS AT ALL: THIS PROGRAM FOLDS NO CASE. Searched, not assumed: FUNCTION UPPER-CASE, FUNCTION LOWER-CASE and INSPECT ... CONVERTING appear NOWHERE in the 572 lines of COBIL00C. The program normalises nothing. Instead it ENUMERATES both letter cases as stacked WHEN clauses, and it does so THREE TIMES OVER in this one EVALUATE: 'Y' at :174 with 'y' at :175, 'N' at :178 with 'n' at :179, and SPACES at :182 with LOW-VALUES at :183. Contrast COSGN00C, which in the same repository and the same release does the opposite - COSGN00C.cbl:132 is MOVE FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(USERIDI OF COSGN0AI) and :135 is the same for PASSWDI, applied unconditionally before any comparison, so its screen accepts any casing through a single arm. Two programs, two opposite conventions for the same problem. That is an INHERITED LEGACY INCONSISTENCY AND IT IS PRESERVED, NOT HARMONISED (practice B5). No upper-casing step is added to COBIL00C to make the two agree: folding the character would change observable behaviour, and it would also delete a branch - the 'n' clause would become unreachable and the arm's second half would silently stop existing. THE PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS SHARPER THAN IT LOOKS. Because the program enumerates rather than folds, it recognises EXACTLY SIX SPELLINGS: 'Y', 'y', 'N', 'n', a space and LOW-VALUES. Anything else at all - a mixed-case or accented variant, an upper-case letter from another alphabet, 'YES', 'no' truncated to 'n' by the one-character field notwithstanding - reaches WHEN OTHER at :185 and is treated as AN ERROR, NOT AS A DECLINE: 'Invalid value. Valid values are (Y/N)...' with the cursor moved to CONFIRML. That path is sibling case12's, and the distinction is behavioural rather than cosmetic - an error re-prompts with text and leaves the typed fields in place, whereas this arm clears the screen and says nothing. A translation that folded case would have collapsed the two outcomes for every casing variant it newly accepted. WHY THE PAIR IS NOT ONE CASE. COBOL WHEN clauses do not fall through, they stack, so :178 and :179 are two spellings of one arm and the body at :180-181 is written once. A faithful translation expresses that as one guard with two disjuncts, and THE SECOND DISJUNCT IS WHAT THIS CASE DRIVES. A translation that implemented only the upper-case spelling would satisfy every assertion case13 makes and would still be wrong for every user who typed a lower-case letter; with only one of the two cases shipped, half of every stacked WHEN in this program would go unexercised and gate G30 would be half satisfied while reporting a diff count of zero. That is the whole reason case13/case14 and case15/case16 exist as pairs. ORDER OF ARRIVAL AT THE ARM, AND THE ORDER IS ITSELF AN EXPECTATION. 'n' reaches its clause only because :174 WHEN 'Y' and :175 WHEN 'y' were tested first and did not match, AND because :178 WHEN 'N' did not match either - so this case sits one position further into the ordered switch than case13 does. It is matched before :182 WHEN SPACES, :183 WHEN LOW-VALUES and :185 WHEN OTHER are ever considered. An EVALUATE is ordered: first match wins, WHEN OTHER is last and is the default. A translation that reordered the clauses, or that let one fall through into the next, would be a different program even where the fields it sent happened to agree (gate G30). IN SOURCE ORDER, AND THE ORDER IS THE BEHAVIOUR. :156 SET CONF-PAY-NO TO TRUE, before any validation, so the confirmation flag is already 'N' when the switch is entered and this arm never needs to set it. :158-167 EVALUATE TRUE tests ACTIDINI OF COBIL0AI against SPACES and LOW-VALUES; the account identifier 00000000001 is neither, so the first arm is not taken and :165-166 WHEN OTHER / CONTINUE is - a genuine no-op arm, and no error flag. :169 IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON opens. :170-171 MOVE ACTIDINI OF COBIL0AI TO ACCT-ID / XREF-ACCT-ID: ONE MOVE WITH TWO RECEIVERS, a PIC X(11) sender into two PIC 9(11) receivers, and THERE IS NO NUMERIC VALIDATION ANYWHERE IN THIS PROGRAM. None is added here (practice B5). Both keys are set even though this arm reads nothing, because the statement precedes the switch. WHAT THE ARM DOES, IN THE ORDER IT DOES IT, AND WHY DECLINING PRODUCES NO TEXT AT ALL. :180 PERFORM CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN. That paragraph at :552-555 is exactly two performs, in this order: INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS then SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN. INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS at :560-566 moves -1 into ACTIDINL OF COBIL0AI and then moves SPACES into ACTIDINI, CURBALI, CONFIRMI and WS-MESSAGE - FOUR RECEIVERS AND NO MORE. It does NOT touch TRNNAME, TITLE01, CURDATE, PGMNAME, TITLE02, CURTIME or ERRMSG. THEN :181 MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG - after the send, not before it. The consequence is the headline observable and it is a negative one: SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN at :289-301 performs POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :291 and then, at :293, moves WS-MESSAGE into ERRMSGO OF COBIL0AO - and :566 had just cleared WS-MESSAGE, so the eighty bytes moved are eighty blanks and the seventy-eight that survive the picture difference are SEVENTY-EIGHT BLANKS. ERRMSG is not one of the four fields :563-565 clear; it does not need to be, because it is written from the field that was. Any expectation here containing explanatory text - a 'Payment cancelled', a 'Payment declined', anything - would be a fabrication, and it would also be proof that :180 and :181 had been read in the wrong order. The error flag exists on this arm solely to suppress the three stages that follow. THE INBOUND 'n' DOES NOT SURVIVE THE ARM, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF SENDING IT. :565 clears CONFIRMI, so CONFIRMO comes back as ONE SPACE - the lower-case letter that selected the clause is gone from the screen the terminal receives. Likewise :563 clears ACTIDINI, so ACTIDINO comes back as ELEVEN SPACES. Both blank expectations are therefore assertions that the clear wiped values that were GENUINELY THERE - 00000000001 and 'n' - and not tautologies about fields that arrived empty. A case that had sent a blank confirmation would have proved nothing about :565, and would in any event have taken :182-184 instead of this arm. EXACTLY ONE SEND, AND THAT COUNT IS AN ASSERTION. The send at :180 is the only one this path issues. :197 IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON and :208 IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON both find the flag on - :181 set it - so the 'You have nothing to pay...' test at :198-205 does not run, the CONF-PAY-YES payment sequence at :210-235 does not run, the 'Confirm to make a bill payment...' prompt at :237-239 does not run, and the unconditional PERFORM SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN at :242 IS NEVER REACHED. One send, therefore, and not two: the completed payment sends twice, once from the WRITE success arm at :532 and once from :242, and a model that carried a single screen could not tell the two paths apart. The list length is compared, so a second send here would be a difference in its own right. WHAT CURBALO CARRIES, WHY IT IS FOURTEEN SPACES, AND WHY THIS IS THE SAME DETERMINATION case12 AND case13 RECORD RATHER THAN A NEW ONE. END-EVALUATE is at :191 and the END-IF of the :169 guard is at :195, so :193 MOVE ACCT-CURR-BAL TO WS-CURR-BAL and :194 MOVE WS-CURR-BAL TO CURBALI OF COBIL0AI are the last two statements of the stage-two block and they RUN ON EVERY ARM OF THE SWITCH - including this one, which has already raised the flag and, uniquely, has already SENT THE SCREEN. READ-ACCTDAT-FILE at :343-372 is reached only from :177 and :184, neither of which is on this arm, so the WORKING-STORAGE ACCOUNT-RECORD that COPY CVACT01Y brings in at :80 is NEVER POPULATED FROM A DATASET and :193 edits an area the program never filled. The transmitted value, however, is settled by ORDER rather than by content: CURBALI is written at exactly two sites in the whole program - :564 inside INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS, which ran, and :194, which had NOT yet run when the send took place - so the field that went down the line is the fourteen spaces :564 put there. CURBALO is accordingly FOURTEEN SPACES. THE SAME CONSTRUCT MUST NOT YIELD TWO CONCLUSIONS, so this is case12's and case13's determination reused verbatim and not re-derived. The provenance nuance is worth repeating: in case12 those spaces are an UNTOUCHED field, because WHEN OTHER clears nothing; here, exactly as in case13, they are a DELIBERATELY CLEARED field, blanked by :564 and then overwritten by :194 after transmission. Same bytes, two different facts, and neither of them is a zero balance. THE POST-SEND EDIT, AND THE ONE LIMIT OF STATIC DERIVATION IN THIS CASE. :193-194 do execute, and the state they leave behind is not what the screen carried. app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy declares ACCT-CURR-BAL as PIC S9(10)V99 and carries NO VALUE CLAUSE on any of its twelve named items or on its trailing FILLER X(178), and COBOL does not define the content of a WORKING-STORAGE item that has none - so THE EXACT BYTE PATTERN THE LEGACY PROGRAM WOULD HAVE EDITED AT :193 IS NOT DETERMINABLE BY STATIC READING, and no honest static derivation can name it. This case therefore asserts nothing about it, which is why the expectation is safe: the value never reaches the wire. The Java side is nonetheless deterministic rather than accidental, which practice B7 requires - billing.BillPaymentService.PaymentState begins with an initialised 300-byte account area whose balance reads 0.00, modelling IBM Enterprise COBOL's binary-zero initialisation of a VALUE-less item, where a numeric-display field of X'00' bytes read under the usual rules is a positive zero - so :193 renders '+0000000000.00' into the fourteen positions of WS-CURR-BAL PIC +9999999999.99 [COBIL00C.cbl:56] and :194 moves it into CURBALI, both AFTER the snapshot. That reading of an unfilled record area is AN EXPLICITLY DOCUMENTED INTERPRETATION AND NOT A CERTAINTY - the same caveat case12 and case13 carry, repeated here rather than quietly inherited. NO ARITHMETIC IS PERFORMED ON THIS PATH, stated rather than left as a silent absence because a reader who sees a balance field might reasonably expect a computation behind it. The program's only COMPUTE is at :234, COMPUTE ACCT-CURR-BAL = ACCT-CURR-BAL - TRAN-AMT, inside the CONF-PAY-YES sequence this arm suppresses. Where the numeric policy does apply it is named explicitly rather than implied (practice B8): ACCT-CURR-BAL is a BigDecimal at SCALE EXACTLY 2 and never a double or a float (AAP rule R4, gate G23), and any store into it truncates with RoundingMode.DOWN - never HALF_UP and never HALF_EVEN - because the keyword ROUNDED appears ZERO TIMES in all twenty-eight programs, so truncation is the only faithful mode (AAP rule R2). The receiving edit mask is PIC +9999999999.99, fourteen positions being a sign, ten integer digits, a point and two fraction digits, which is an exact fit for the fourteen-character CURBAL screen field. Gates G24 and G28 have no subject here. NO DATASET IS TOUCHED, AND THAT IS ASSERTED POSITIVELY RATHER THAN BY OMISSION. The four file operations of this program - READ-ACCTDAT-FILE at :343, UPDATE-ACCTDAT-FILE at :375, READ-CXACAIX-FILE at :406 and the browse-and-write sequence at :211-235 - are all reached from PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, and this arm reaches none of them. inputs is therefore EMPTY: no fixture is seeded, because seeding a row would assert a read the COBOL does not make and would put gate G16's cardxref 36-to-50 pad in the path of a case that reads no cross-reference, which is also why normalisations is empty. expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are empty for the same reason. expectedDatasets, by contrast, is NOT empty, and the difference between an empty list and four zero-row declarations is the difference between saying nothing and saying nothing happened: a dataset-level expectation of ZERO ROWS is the one assertion no row expectation can make, because a dataset holding no row has no row to address. TRANSACT is declared on both channels at zero rows and 350 bytes, the width app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy gives TRAN-RECORD, and ACCTDAT on both channels at zero rows and 300 bytes, the width app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy gives ACCOUNT-RECORD. Pinning the widths matters precisely because the datasets are empty - an empty 350-byte master and an empty 300-byte master are not interchangeable just because both are empty - and pinning their existence at zero rows is what makes 'the payment did not happen' a finding rather than an assumption. Gates G19, G21, G45 and G47 have no subject: no record is written, no FILLER is serialised, no alternate index is read and no FileStatus arm is taken. NO MESSAGE IS EMITTED, AND THE BLANK LINE IS ASSERTED EXACTLY ONCE. expectedMessages is EMPTY, and it is empty by derivation. All six DISPLAY statements in the program - :366, :397, :430, :461, :490 and :541 - sit in the WHEN OTHER arm of a file operation, and this arm performs no file operation, so nothing is displayed. The blank error line is asserted where screen text belongs, as ERRMSGO on the send that produced it; repeating it on a message channel would assert the same seventy-eight bytes twice while claiming an emission the program never made - which is also why a SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 entry of seventy-eight blanks is deliberately NOT declared here. One note on how this case reads against its own brief: the brief asks for 'exactly one entry, with a blank 78-byte error line', and that is what is delivered - exactly one SEND whose seventy-eight-byte error line is blank. Expressed instead as one EmittedMessage it would have contradicted gate G18, because the emitted-line list is compared by count as well as by content and this path emits none, so the reconciliation is recorded here rather than resolved silently. It is case13's reconciliation, reached the same way for the same construct, which is required of a case whose only substantive difference is one inbound character. STATELESSNESS. EIBCALEN is 218 - the 160 bytes app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy declares for CARDDEMO-COMMAREA plus the 58 bytes of the CDEMO-CB00-INFO group COBIL00C.cbl:64-72 appends in place. CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives as 1, which is what :112 tests to find CDEMO-PGM-REENTER true and route to :124 RECEIVE-BILLPAY-SCREEN and the ENTER arm at :126-127, so it is the one commarea item the request declares. It LEAVES AS 1 as well: no XCTL occurs on this arm, RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN is never performed and its MOVE ZEROS TO CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT at :280 is not reached, so the next invocation takes the re-entry arm again. That is the REENTER half of gate G38 - both halves of the context flag are exercised across this directory - and the sixteen navigation spans are pinned in full precisely because PROCESS-ENTER-KEY writes none of them: they travel back exactly as they arrived, which is only assertable because the conversation state travels in the payload and not in a session (gate G37, AAP rule R6). Control falls out of the EVALUATE to EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) at :146-149, which is why the termination is RETURN_TRANSID; and because no XCTL is reached, no next program is named and gate G40 has no subject. NO ATTRIBUTE IS SET, AND THE ATTRIBUTE MAP MUST STAY EMPTY. COBIL00C copies NEITHER CSSETATY NOR CSSTRPFY - its COPY list at :63-85 is COCOM01Y, COBIL00, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CVACT01Y, CVACT03Y, CVTRA05Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - and DFHRED appears NOWHERE in its 572 lines, so there is no red-and-asterisk error highlight to expect on any path, let alone one that sends a blank message line. The only attribute byte the program ever writes is the DFHGREEN of :526, on the transaction-WRITE success arm, and this arm writes no transaction, so the ERRMSGC override does not apply and the send carries no attributes and no DFHGREEN. Highlighting here is limited to the cursor, and a cursor is an xxxL length item: :562 moves -1 into ACTIDINL, so the cursor is declared as ACTIDINL through cursorField and NOT as a payload member - and it is ACTIDINL rather than the CONFIRML that case12's error arm sets at :189, even though it was the confirmation field that was typed, because :562 is what this arm runs. The payload members are the xxxI and xxxO items of app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY at the widths their PICTURE clauses declare - and the xxxL, xxxF and xxxA items on the input side and the xxxC, xxxP, xxxH and xxxV items on the output side are validation and highlight metadata that never appear as fields (practice B11). UNIT KIND, AND WHY THE SEND CARRIES FOUR FIELDS RATHER THAN TEN. unitKind is SERVICE, so the unit is billing.BillPaymentService.processEnterKey - the translation of PROCESS-ENTER-KEY from :154 onwards, which is where the EVALUATE CONFIRMI this case selects actually lives, and where the stacked pair is spelt as a single guard with two disjuncts of which this case drives the SECOND. The service is constructed through its own constructor and called as a plain Java object: no HTTP, no MockMvc, no TestRestTemplate, no servlet container, no JobLauncher and no application context anywhere in the path, which is what gate G51 asks for and what makes an ordered switch assertable without a transport in the way. The send it records therefore carries THE FOUR ITEMS THIS PARAGRAPH AND SEND-BILLPAY-SCREEN WRITE THEMSELVES: ACTIDINO at its declared eleven characters, CURBALO at fourteen, CONFIRMO at one and ERRMSGO at seventy-eight. The header six - TRNNAMEO 'CB00', PGMNAMEO 'COBIL00C', TITLE01O and TITLE02O at their PIC X(40) width from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22, CURDATEO as MM/DD/YY and CURTIMEO as HH:MM:SS from the groups app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy assembles - are POPULATE-HEADER-INFO's at :319-338 and belong to the controller projection, so a SERVICE case does not claim them; case06 pins all ten because it is a CONTROLLER_POJO case. They are still repopulated by :291 on this path, and case06 is where that is asserted. The four items are addressed as xxxO names because app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY:79 declares COBIL0AO REDEFINES COBIL0AI, so input and output share one span - a MOVE SPACES to ACTIDINI is observable as SPACES in ACTIDINO - and :298 sends FROM(COBIL0AO). WHAT THE REQUEST SEEDS, AND WHY. Only ACTIDIN, which carries IC, and CONFIRM are UNPROT in app/bms/COBIL00.bms, so those two are the only items a RECEIVE can carry and the only two the request declares; CURBALI is protected and can never be typed. ACTIDINI carries 00000000001, the same real key case13 uses, taken from app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt, so the case is production-shaped even though nothing is read with it - and carrying a non-blank identifier is what makes :159 take its WHEN OTHER arm and the switch reachable at all. CONFIRMI carries 'n' - ONE LOWER-CASE CHARACTER at its declared PIC X(1) width, and THE SINGLE SUBSTANTIVE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THIS CASE AND case13, which carries 'N'. DETERMINISM. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:32, the instant the program's own version footer at :571 carries, and every case in this directory pins that same instant; the header date and time are derived from an injected Clock through common.DateHeader and never from a captured now (practice B7). Nothing on this path renders either one - POPULATE-HEADER-INFO's output belongs to the controller projection - and GET-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP at :249-267 is unreached, so no twenty-six-byte timestamp is produced either; the instant is pinned regardless, because a case that left the clock free would be one Clock change away from a difference it never meant to assert. US-ASCII is named explicitly rather than left to a platform default, which for a nine-fixture ASCII corpus and a twelve-dataset EBCDIC one is the difference between a comparison and a coincidence. Every blank in the expectation is written out as an explicit run of spaces at its declared width - eleven, fourteen, one and seventy-eight - and never as null or as an empty string (practice B1). PROVENANCE. Every value above is STATICALLY DERIVED - read out of the COBOL paragraph that produces it, principally app/cbl/COBIL00C.cbl:178-181, :193-194, :289-301 and :552-566, and cross-checked against the xxxI and xxxO PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COBIL00.CPY, the DFHMDF definitions and 24-by-80 DFHMDI of app/bms/COBIL00.bms, the S9(10)V99 balance of app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy and the 160-byte layout of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy - and it WAS NOT CAPTURED FROM A LIVE COBOL EXECUTION, not one byte of it, because such a capture is empirically impossible in this environment: no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, no Language Environment CEE services, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR absent from the repository - which is why the DFHENTER mnemonic this case declares comes from common.CicsAid, the single reproduction of DFHAID, rather than from a copybook. AAP 0.7.6 documents eight verified blockers, 0.9.11 records the substitution as risk R-A escalated for confirmation rather than absorbed, and 0.9.12 records the missing copybooks as risk R-D. The one place this case reaches the limit of static derivation is the uninitialised ACCOUNT-RECORD of :193, flagged above as a documented interpretation rather than a certainty; it is also the one place where nothing is asserted, so the limit costs the expectation nothing. No user rule governs this file - review_rules returns exactly 'No user rules provided' - which AAP 0.10 treats as a reason to hold to enterprise practice rather than as licence to lower the bar, so B1, B3, B5, B7, B8, B11 and B12 are the constraints this case is written against, and B3 in particular: app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms and app/data were read and not one byte of them was written.
